name: Shenzhen Streets for Cyclists: Good or Bad on Three Dimensions
description:
Method replication: participants imagine cycling at 30 Shenzhen street scenes, each shown as four views around one spot, and judge each as Good or Bad for public security, traffic safety and scenic beauty; the images are not the paper's stimuli (50 newly fetched Baidu street views in Nanshan, Futian and Luohu, four directions at 90° field of view, cropped to remove the camera car).

Original study: Zeng, Gong, Wu, Zhuang & Li (2024), International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation 128, 103739. Baidu street views were taken at the midpoint of every road in central Shenzhen (10,194 points, four 90° frames, 2016–2021). In the authors' rating software, 50 volunteers (equal gender split) each viewed 500 four-view scenes and marked each Good or Bad on the three dimensions (75,000 ratings). K-means SMOTE balanced the classes, a random forest per volunteer mapped the perceptions, and SHAP showed which visual elements mattered.

Differences from the original study: (1) 30 random scenes per participant instead of 500; (2) the four views are shown as a 2 × 2 grid; (3) the short definitions of each dimension are condensed from the paper's text; (4) the cycling-frequency question is added for this template.
author: Zeng, Gong, Wu, Zhuang & Li
